name: Rizal Province Protected Ecological Zones, Sanctuaries & Conservation Buffers

properties.name: Upper Marikina River Basin Protected Landscape (UMRBPL)
properties.municipality: Rodriguez, Antipolo City, Baras, San Mateo, Tanay
properties.legalBasis: Executive Order No. 33 (1904), Presidential Proclamation No. 296 (2011), Republic Act No. 11038
properties.legalNote: Protected Landscape under RA 11038 (E-NIPAS). Encompasses 26,125.60 hectares across Boso-Boso, Tayabasan, Wawa, Montalban, and Puray sub-watersheds. Timber cutting, unauthorized quarrying, and slash-and-burn (kaingin) carry statutory penalties.

properties.name: Kaliwa River Forest Reserve (KRFR)
properties.legalBasis: Presidential Proclamation No. 573 (1969) / Initial NIPAS Component
properties.legalNote: Covers ~27,608 hectares spanning Tanay (Rizal) and Gen. Nakar (Quezon). Protects the headwaters of Kaliwa River. Logging, forest burning, and illegal road cuts carry strict penalties under PD 705 and RA 11038.

properties.name: Pamitinan Protected Landscape (PPL)
properties.legalBasis: Presidential Proclamation No. 901 (1996), Republic Act No. 11038
properties.legalNote: 608.64 hectares encompassing Wawa Gorge, Mt. Pamitinan, Mt. Binacayan, Wawa Dam, and Pamitinan Cave in Sitio Wawa. Any rock extraction, slope alteration, or waste disposal is legally prohibited.

properties.name: Hinulugang Taktak Protected Landscape
properties.legalBasis: Proclamation No. 330 (1952), Republic Act No. 6964 (1990), Proclamation No. 412 (2000), RA 11038
properties.legalNote: 3.20 hectares of historical waterfall riparian basin along upper Taktak River. Direct wastewater discharge, commercial littering, and unauthorized building structures are strictly prohibited.

properties.name: National Park, Wildlife Sanctuary & Game Preserve (Proc. 1636)
properties.municipality: Rodriguez, San Mateo, Antipolo, Baras, Tanay, Pililla
properties.legalNote: ~46,310-hectare multi-provincial reserve safeguarding the Sierra Madre biodiversity corridor. Hunting, wildlife trapping, slash-and-burn, and unpermitted resource gathering carry statutory criminal penalties.

properties.name: La Mesa Watershed Reservation Buffer (Rizal Flank)
properties.legalBasis: Presidential Proclamation No. 1336 & Executive Order No. 601
properties.legalNote: Critical eastern buffer protection for the Greater Manila potable water reservoir. Land conversion, industrial runoff, illegal excavation, and trash dumping along tributary streams carry immediate cease-and-desist mandates.

properties.name: Rayap Fish Sanctuary (LLDA Central Bay Fish Sanctuary)
properties.legalBasis: Republic Act No. 4826, LLDA Board Resolution No. 136 (Series of 2000)
properties.legalNote: 5,000 hectares covering ~5% of Laguna de Bay in Central Bay. Demarcated from Punta (Jalajala) to Habagatan/Rayap (Talim Island) to Malahi/Pihan/Bunga islets, Nagsabya Point (Cardona), and Bayugo (Jalajala). Commercial fishpens, motorized trawling, and toxic dumping strictly banned.

properties.name: Laguna de Bay Protected Shoreland Buffer Zone (12.5m Elevation)
properties.municipality: Taytay, Angono, Binangonan, Cardona, Morong, Baras, Tanay, Pililla, Jalajala
barangays: Lakeshore littoral zone across all 9 coastal municipalities
properties.legalBasis: LLDA ZOMAP, Presidential Decree No. 1067 (Water Code), LLDA Res. 136 (s. 2000)
properties.legalNote: Public shoreland buffer at or below 12.50m elevation across all 9 lakeshore LGUs of Rizal. Protects littoral wetlands and regulates flood plains. Solid waste dumping, illegal reclamation, and untreated wastewater runoff are prohibited.

properties.name: Mounts Irid–Angilo & Binuang Key Biodiversity Area (KBA 9720)
properties.legalBasis: DENR-BMB National Key Biodiversity Area Directory (KBA No. 9720), RA 8371 (IPRA)
properties.legalNote: 170,572-hectare regional KBA centered on Mt. Irid (1,469 MASL), the highest peak in Rizal. Overlaps Dumagat-Remontado ancestral domain. Poaching endangered flora/fauna, commercial logging, and unpermitted mining are strictly penalized.

properties.name: Masungi Georeserve & Karst Conservation Area
properties.legalBasis: DENR-Masungi Reforestation Agreement / Karst Conservation, DAO 96-37
properties.legalNote: ~2,700-hectare ancient Paleocene–Eocene limestone karst formation and watershed headwater divide between Marikina and Kaliwa. Quarrying, blasting, unauthorized fencing, and land speculation are strictly prohibited under special conservation status.

properties.name: Angono–Binangonan Petroglyphs Site & Micro-Forest Reserve
properties.legalBasis: Presidential Decree No. 260 (1973, National Cultural Treasure), Proclamation No. 2146
properties.legalNote: Declared National Cultural Treasure. Protects the oldest known prehistoric rock art in the Philippines and its secondary forest buffer. Vandalism, rock face defacement, quarrying, and unauthorized excavations carry severe statutory penalties.

properties.name: Mount Tagapo Local Forest & Ecotourism Zone
properties.legalNote: 438 MASL volcanic peak forming the central spine of Talim Island. Tree cutting, open burning (siga), quarrying, and unauthorized trail blazes carry mandatory municipal statutory fines.

properties.name: Mount Sembrano Watershed & Forest Reserve
properties.legalBasis: Municipal Environmental Ordinances (Pililla & Jalajala), Upland Watershed Co-Management Framework
properties.legalNote: 743–745 MASL volcanic ridge separating Pililla and Jalajala. Protects headwaters of Manggahan and seasonal streams feeding eastern Laguna de Bay. Kaingin, illegal charcoal making, and stream pollution strictly banned.

properties.name: Mount Balagbag–Mount Maranat Foothills
properties.legalBasis: Rodriguez Municipal Ecotourism & Watershed Buffer Resolution, Southern Ipo-Angat Buffer Corridor
properties.legalNote: Upland headwater corridor in northwestern Rodriguez bordering San Jose del Monte (Bulacan) and Ipo Watershed. Unlicensed land clearing, off-road vegetation destruction, and waste abandonment are prohibited.

properties.name: Daranak & Batlag Falls Ecotourism Sanctuary
properties.legalBasis: Tanay Municipal Environmental Protection Ordinance No. 2, Tanay Ecotourism Master Plan
properties.legalNote: ~150 hectares surrounding Daranak River, Batlag Falls, and Calinawan Cave. Discharging untreated contaminants into streamways, defacing rock formations, and littering carry statutory municipal penalties.
